test.name: A bounded ask is not routed into the question/plan chain
test.description: The other direction of the same rule. 'Transcribe image <id> for me' asks for ONE deliverable, so the 'Bounded request or job' section must stop it entering the question-selection / research-plan chain that a job walks. The project has an objective and zero questions, so a router that ignored the section would call question-selection first -- exactly what ut_research_011 asserts for an open ask. Here that call is the FAILURE. GRADING: deterministic. `routes-to:image-reader` makes `test_routes_to_expected_skill` assert the first hand-off from hook records, which the judge cannot see (agent spawns are absent from `skills_invoked`). image-reader is the destination because its own description owns 'transcribe this register page' / 'OCR this scan', and the router holds no `image_transcribe`, so inline is not an option. Paired with ut_research_019 (open ask -> question-selection) so both directions are pinned deterministically: neither passes a body that classifies everything one way. The message NAMES an image because `image-reader`'s invocation contract requires an `imageId`; without one the correct router behaviour is to ask which page, which makes no hand-off at all and reds the deterministic validator on a message-authoring choice rather than on the rule.

judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST test. The reply must show the router treating this as one deliverable: it must NOT invoke question-selection or research-plan, and must not start deriving research questions from the objective.

A transcription is named in the skill's own bounded list, and the body sends it to @plugin:image-reader. Walking the routing table from the top -- which on this scenario reaches question-selection -- is the failure. The hand-off itself is asserted deterministically; grade only the framing of the reply.
Do not grade transcription quality -- no record is attached in this scenario. Grade only whether the request was treated as bounded.
